scope.market_definition: The leukemia therapeutics market encompasses the development, distribution, and sale of medications specifically designed to treat leukemia, a type of cancer affecting blood cells. Key participants include pharmaceutical manufacturers, distributors, wholesalers, and various service providers involved in the therapeutic supply chain, operating on a global scale.

value_chain_layers.description: This layer involves the production of leukemia therapeutics, including both branded and generic drugs.
This layer includes the logistics and distribution of leukemia therapeutics to healthcare providers and pharmacies.
This layer includes organizations that provide support services related to leukemia therapeutics.

# We are now Cencora. Our shared identity unites us.

Cencora brings the companies and services of AmerisourceBergen together under one new name.

[ Meet Cencora ][86]
[A banner that says We Are Cencora on a pink and purple background]

# Marketplace gives pharmacies access to thousands of uniquely curated front-of-store products

We’re reimagining the procurement process by enabling pharmacies to source all the products they
need from front to back through one convenient platform.
[ Learn more ][87]
[A person viewing the Marketplace homepage on their laptop]

## We are united in our responsibility
## to create healthier futures.

As we pursue our purpose, we make a positive impact on the health of people and animals around the
world.

### Pharmaceutical distribution solutions

Our wholesale and specialty distribution services ensure that crucial medications efficiently,
reliably and securely reach their destinations every day.
[ Learn more ][88]
[AB_1Card_03]

### Manufacturer solutions

In addition to distribution and logistics, we help pharmaceutical manufacturers bring their products
to market – and assist with each step from pre-commercial and clinical trial to broad market
availability and patient adherence.
[ Learn more ][89]
[AB_2_3_Card_03]

### Provider solutions

Our solutions power patient care for pharmacies, physician practices, hospitals and health systems.
[ Learn more ][90]
[AB_2_3_Card_05]

### Animal health solutions

We deliver distribution, technology and innovation for veterinarians, livestock producers and
manufacturers to make a meaningful difference in their businesses and the health of animals.
[ Learn more ][91]

# Oncology, answered.

Flatiron Health answers oncology’s toughest questions by learning from the experience of every
person with cancer.

We combine high-fidelity data with AI that’s powered by human expertise. That means faster answers,
stronger decisions, and better outcomes for every patient.

Explore our solutions:

[For Life Sciences][4][For the Point of Care][5]
[map-dots-random-staggered]

Every patient story shapes the next.

Our global oncology engine captures data from millions of cancer patients around the world, directly
at the source, and transforms it into actionable insights across the entire oncology ecosystem.

Flatiron real-world data has informed 2,000+ publications—and counting

healthy.

### From Phone Tag to Push Notifications: How Four Health Systems Closed the Loop on Critical Lab
### Communication

July 06, 2026
Four health systems are among those that have replaced phone calls for critical lab result
communication with Epic push notifications, achieving acknowledgement times under one
minute—compared to an average of seven to twelve minutes previously. Lab staff save approximately
ten minutes per result, which adds up to enough time saved at one organization for 15 full-time
staff members to focus on higher-value work. Clinicians acted faster on critical results, where
every minute matters.
[Read the full story on EpicShare →][8]
[Providing Pain Relief for Sickle Cell Crises Faster with Personal, Portable Care Plans]

### Providing Pain Relief for Sickle Cell Crises Faster with Personal, Portable Care Plans

June 22, 2026
Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust developed a digital sickle cell care program to improve
tracking and transparency of emergency pain management. The program includes personalized emergency
care plans and an ED order set. Patients went from having no digital care plans to 89% coverage, and
active patient portal usage among people with sickle cell disease increased from 43% to 58%.
[Read the full story on EpicShare →][9]
[Using Telecritical Care to Reduce ICU Mortality]

### Using Telecritical Care to Reduce ICU Mortality

June 15, 2026
To provide expert overnight critical care, Kaiser Permanente Northern California implemented a
telecritical care program that connects remote intensivists and nurses to ICUs through real-time
monitoring, camera feeds, and instant communication. Today, the program is in use across 18 ICUs and
is associated with a 7% reduction in adjusted mortality.
[Read the full story on EpicShare →][10]

### AI Coding Assistant Reduces Chart Review Time by 20%, Freeing Coders for Higher-Value Work

June 08, 2026
After implementing Epic’s AI Professional Billing Coding Assistant, coders at Baptist Health in
Jacksonville, Florida spend 20% less time reviewing charts—an estimated $924,000 in annual labor
savings. Clean claim rates and coder productivity have also improved.
[Read the full story on EpicShare →][11]

# Marketplace gives pharmacies access to thousands of uniquely curated front-of-store products

We’re reimagining the procurement process by enabling pharmacies to source all the products they
need from front to back through one convenient platform.
[ Learn more ][87]
[A person viewing the Marketplace homepage on their laptop]

## We are united in our responsibility
## to create healthier futures.

As we pursue our purpose, we make a positive impact on the health of people and animals around the
world.

### Pharmaceutical distribution solutions

Our wholesale and specialty distribution services ensure that crucial medications efficiently,
reliably and securely reach their destinations every day.
[ Learn more ][88]
[AB_1Card_03]

### Manufacturer solutions

In addition to distribution and logistics, we help pharmaceutical manufacturers bring their products
to market – and assist with each step from pre-commercial and clinical trial to broad market
availability and patient adherence.
[ Learn more ][89]
[AB_2_3_Card_03]

### Provider solutions

Our solutions power patient care for pharmacies, physician practices, hospitals and health systems.
[ Learn more ][90]
[AB_2_3_Card_05]

### Animal health solutions

We deliver distribution, technology and innovation for veterinarians, livestock producers and
manufacturers to make a meaningful difference in their businesses and the health of animals.
[ Learn more ][91]

## Réseau européen de concurrence (ECN)

Créé en mai 2004, le Réseau européen de concurrence (ECN) fête cette année son 20ème anniversaire.
Entre mai 2004 et décembre 2023, les autorités nationales de concurrence ont rendu plus de 1 700
décisions fondées sur l'article 101 et/ou l'article 102. Les autorités nationales de concurrence ont
lancé en moyenne 140 enquêtes et adopté 75 décisions chaque année.

d'emmener l'auditeur dans les coulisses de ses enquêtes, au cœur de scandales économiques impliquant
des entreprises mondiales.

## Redefining Healthcare Delivery

We are everywhere healthcare happens – and everywhere it is going, with essential solutions in the
hospital, physician’s office and other sites of care. Every day, millions of patients and healthcare
providers rely on our unmatched portfolio of connected solutions, medical devices, and advanced
injectable technologies to help deliver smarter, more personalized care. Together, we are redefining

## The future of healthcare is connected

Healthcare is at a turning point. Clinicians face growing workloads, while patients increasingly
expect seamless, coordinated experiences. Despite recent advances in technology, medical devices and
clinical systems continue to be isolated from each other, preventing effective data sharing,
creating inefficiencies and increasing the potential for gaps in care. The future demands better
connectivity.
* **100,000** nurses left the workforce during the COVID-19 pandemic
* **610,338** nurses reported intent to leave by 2027

[Cancer History Project On ][80]
What is the
Cancer History Project

The goal of the Cancer History Project is twofold: to collect and preserve the history of cancer
research, and to spark rigorous discussion of the achievements of the past half-century.

Created to mark the 50th anniversary of the National Cancer Act of 1971, the Cancer History Project
is a free historical resource that places a vast, expertly curated collection of primary sources and
authoritative interpretations within easy reach of researchers, medical professionals, students,
policy-makers, and patients.

The Cancer History Project is a new way of preserving history: collaboratively curated by the
institutions and people who shaped it.

## About

### ESMO Open

[[Cover Image - ESMO Open, Volume 11, Issue 7]][78]

*ESMO Open* is the European Society for Medical Oncology's online-only, peer-reviewed open access
journal, dedicated to publishing high-quality medical research and educational content from all
disciplines of oncology, with a focus on innovative clinical and translational cancer research. The
Journal aims to maximize industry networks to curate and disseminate preclinical or translational
data. We hope to bridge the gap between basic research and clinical applications, facilitating the
translation of groundbreaking discoveries into tangible advancements in cancer care. Our platform
will serve as a catalyst for innovation, nurturing the dialogue between academia, industry, and
clinical practice.

### ESMO

[ESMO  Opens in new window][79]   is the European Society for Medical Oncology. Representing over
50,000 members globally, ESMO is a reference for oncology education and information.

Founded in 1975, ESMO has European roots with a global reach. Home for all oncology stakeholders,
ESMO connects professionals with diverse expertise and experience. Its education and information
resources support an integrated multi-professional approach to cancer care, from a medical oncology
perspective.

ESMO seeks to erase boundaries in cancer care, whether between countries or specialities, and pursue
its mission

that support efficient documentation, informed decision-making and more streamlined diabetes visits.

Whether it's the challenge of a marathon or the sprint to save lives with specialized care, these
stories highlight what it means to be Henry.

## ** Former employee relies on Henry Ford Family after first colonoscopy reveals cancer**

For more than two decades, Brooke Wessman took great pride in working for Henry Ford Health. As
someone who prioritizes healthy living — exercise, clean eating and routine screenings, Brooke
received a colon cancer screening at age 45 with a Cologuard test. She was surprised when the
results detected altered DNA and/or blood, a possible sign of precancerous polyps or colon cancer.
[ Read Brooke's Story ][89]

## ** Back in flow following vascular surgery**

When Eric’s left bicep swelled up so large that it strained his shirt sleeve, he knew something was
wrong. This sudden development was a shock to Eric, then 39, a West Bloomfield resident. He was
healthy, had lived a very active life and his only previous medical issues were sports injuries when
he was growing up. Following many tests, an ER doctor referred Eric to a vascular surgeon who was
able to figure out what was going on and act quickly.
[ Read Eric's Story ][90]

## ** Nurse practitioner finds alternative treatment to thyroid nodule through RFA procedure**

Lisa Smith had a history of abnormal thyroid labs since she was pregnant with her son around eight
years ago. She also had a family history of thyroid disease, so when it was found that she had a
nodule on her thyroid that was causing it to be hyperactive, she was not surprised. She was hesitant
to undergo treatment because she would need to be on medication long term. But thanks to a new
procedure, she and her doctor were able to take action she was comfortable with.
[ Read Lisa's Story ][91]

#### Detailed Market Analysis

The pharmaceutical industry is undergoing a remarkable digital transformation, supported by concrete
market research and verified statistics. The scale of this transformation is evidenced by the
pharmaceutical digital platform market’s projected growth from $4.92 billion in 2023 to $34.12
billion by 2032, representing a robust CAGR of 24.35%. This growth is driven by widespread cloud
adoption, with approximately 80% of pharmaceutical companies already utilizing cloud computing
solutions and 95% expected to be fully cloud-operational within two years.

The transformation is happening across multiple dimensions, with web-based solutions dominating at
72.27% market share and AI-driven engagement representing 27.05% of patient engagement solutions.
Quality management systems are also evolving, with the market expected to grow from $1.87 billion in
2024 to $3.85 billion by 2030 at a CAGR of 12.99%. This digital evolution is particularly strong in
North America, which holds a 43.6% share in patient engagement solutions and 39% of the quality
management software market. Implementation timelines vary by solution complexity, ranging from 3-6
months for modular SaaS deployments to 9-18 months for full-suite implementations, reflecting the
industry’s methodical approach to digital adoption while maintaining compliance with regulatory
requirements.

### Redness and Sensitivity

One of the most common [post-treatment effects][27] is redness. After treatments like chemical

### Dryness and Peeling

Many facial treatments speed up skin cell turnover. As a result, dryness and peeling are common
during recovery. Patients may notice flaky patches, rough texture, or visible shedding a few days
after treatment. This is especially common after:
* Chemical peels
* Laser resurfacing
* Retinol-based treatments
* Acne correction procedures
Peeling can vary from very mild to more noticeable, depending on the strength of the treatment.
Beauty professionals usually advise patients not to pick or scrub peeling skin. Trying to remove
flaking skin too early may increase irritation or affect results. Instead, clinics often recommend:
* Hydrating moisturizers
* Barrier-repair creams
* Gentle cleansing routines
* Avoiding strong exfoliants
Patients are sometimes surprised that dry skin can appear after treatments designed to improve
hydration or glow. However, temporary dryness is often part of the skin renewal process.

Some treatments can cause temporary inflammation, leading to mild swelling or puffiness. This is
especially common after:
* Injectable treatments
* Facial contouring procedures
* Laser therapies
* Surgical cosmetic procedures
* Microneedling sessions
Swelling is usually most noticeable during the first few days of recovery. Areas around the eyes and
cheeks may appear fuller or tighter than usual. Beauty providers often suggest cold compresses,
hydration, and rest to help reduce puffiness.
Patients are also commonly advised to avoid excessive heat, liquor, or strenuous exercise
immediately after treatment because these activities may increase inflammation. In most cases,
swelling improves gradually as the healing process continues.

### Temporary Breakouts

Some patients experience temporary breakouts during recovery. This can happen when the skin is
adjusting to increased cell turnover or when impurities trapped beneath the surface begin to clear.
Treatments that may occasionally trigger short-term purging include:
* Chemical exfoliation
* Acne facials
* Retinol treatments
* Deep cleansing procedures
Although breakouts can feel frustrating, they are not always a sign that the treatment failed.

important for clinics to closely monitor recovery. If irritation becomes severe or prolonged,
patients may need adjustments to their skincare routine or follow-up care. Professional guidance
during this stage helps prevent patients from overusing harsh acne products that could worsen

## Life-Changing Research

Nemours is leading important pediatric research and clinical trials. We’re preventing and reversing
the course of childhood diseases, improving health care delivery, and keeping children safe and
healthy for generations to come. We partner with renowned medical schools and organizations to find
answers to the most pressing questions in kids’ health. Our discoveries help children in your
community and all over the world.

more. Join us.

## Réseau européen de concurrence (ECN)

Créé en mai 2004, le Réseau européen de concurrence (ECN) fête cette année son 20ème anniversaire.
Entre mai 2004 et décembre 2023, les autorités nationales de concurrence ont rendu plus de 1 700
décisions fondées sur l'article 101 et/ou l'article 102. Les autorités nationales de concurrence ont
lancé en moyenne 140 enquêtes et adopté 75 décisions chaque année.

Cartels & Cie est un podcast dédié aux grandes affaires démantelées par l'Autorité, qui se propose
d'emmener l'auditeur dans les coulisses de ses enquêtes, au cœur de scandales économiques impliquant
des entreprises mondiales.

## The future of healthcare is connected

Healthcare is at a turning point. Clinicians face growing workloads, while patients increasingly
expect seamless, coordinated experiences. Despite recent advances in technology, medical devices and
clinical systems continue to be isolated from each other, preventing effective data sharing,
creating inefficiencies and increasing the potential for gaps in care. The future demands better
connectivity.

What is the
Cancer History Project

The goal of the Cancer History Project is twofold: to collect and preserve the history of cancer
research, and to spark rigorous discussion of the achievements of the past half-century.

Created to mark the 50th anniversary of the National Cancer Act of 1971, the Cancer History Project
is a free historical resource that places a vast, expertly curated collection of primary sources and
authoritative interpretations within easy reach of researchers, medical professionals, students,
policy-makers, and patients.

The Cancer History Project is a new way of preserving history: collaboratively curated by the
institutions and people who shaped it.

## About

### ESMO Open

[[Cover Image - ESMO Open, Volume 11, Issue 7]][78]

*ESMO Open* is the European Society for Medical Oncology's online-only, peer-reviewed open access
journal, dedicated to publishing high-quality medical research and educational content from all
disciplines of oncology, with a focus on innovative clinical and translational cancer research. The
Journal aims to maximize industry networks to curate and disseminate preclinical or translational
data. We hope to bridge the gap between basic research and clinical applications, facilitating the
translation of groundbreaking discoveries into tangible advancements in cancer care. Our platform
will serve as a catalyst for innovation, nurturing the dialogue between academia, industry, and
clinical practice.

### ESMO

[ESMO  Opens in new window][79]   is the European Society for Medical Oncology. Representing over
50,000 members globally, ESMO is a reference for oncology education and information.

Founded in 1975, ESMO has European roots with a global reach. Home for all oncology stakeholders,
ESMO connects professionals with diverse expertise and experience. Its education and information
resources support an integrated multi-professional approach to cancer care, from a medical oncology
perspective.

ESMO seeks to erase boundaries in cancer care, whether between countries or specialities, and pursue
its mission

## [ Glooko Expands EHR Integration Through Xealth: Diabetes Data, Embedded in the EHR ][59]

July 15, 2026

For health systems that use Xealth to manage digital health applications, diabetes data integration
no longer needs to be a tradeoff between workflow simplicity and clinical depth. By deploying
Glooko’s diabetes management EHR integration capabilities through the Xealth platform, healthcare
providers can bring rich diabetes data directly into EHR workflows while preserving the architecture

## ** Former employee relies on Henry Ford Family after first colonoscopy reveals cancer**

For more than two decades, Brooke Wessman took great pride in working for Henry Ford Health. As
someone who prioritizes healthy living — exercise, clean eating and routine screenings, Brooke
received a colon cancer screening at age 45 with a Cologuard test. She was surprised when the
results detected altered DNA and/or blood, a possible sign of precancerous polyps or colon cancer.

## ** Back in flow following vascular surgery**

When Eric’s left bicep swelled up so large that it strained his shirt sleeve, he knew something was
wrong. This sudden development was a shock to Eric, then 39, a West Bloomfield resident. He was
healthy, had lived a very active life and his only previous medical issues were sports injuries when
he was growing up. Following many tests, an ER doctor referred Eric to a vascular surgeon who was
able to figure out what was going on and act quickly.
[ Read Eric's Story ][90]

## ** Nurse practitioner finds alternative treatment to thyroid nodule through RFA procedure**

Lisa Smith had a history of abnormal thyroid labs since she was pregnant with her son around eight
years ago. She also had a family history of thyroid disease, so when it was found that she had a
nodule on her thyroid that was causing it to be hyperactive, she was not surprised. She was hesitant
to undergo treatment because she would need to be on medication long term. But thanks to a new
procedure, she and her doctor were able to take action she was comfortable with.

#### Detailed Market Analysis

The pharmaceutical industry is undergoing a remarkable digital transformation, supported by concrete
market research and verified statistics. The scale of this transformation is evidenced by the
pharmaceutical digital platform market’s projected growth from $4.92 billion in 2023 to $34.12
billion by 2032, representing a robust CAGR of 24.35%. This growth is driven by widespread cloud
adoption, with approximately 80% of pharmaceutical companies already utilizing cloud computing
solutions and 95% expected to be fully cloud-operational within two years.

The transformation is happening across multiple dimensions, with web-based solutions dominating at
72.27% market share and AI-driven engagement representing 27.05% of patient engagement solutions.
Quality management systems are also evolving, with the market expected to grow from $1.87 billion in
2024 to $3.85 billion by 2030 at a CAGR of 12.99%. This digital evolution is particularly strong in
North America, which holds a 43.6% share in patient engagement solutions and 39% of the quality
management software market. Implementation timelines vary by solution complexity, ranging from 3-6
months for modular SaaS deployments to 9-18 months for full-suite implementations, reflecting the
industry’s methodical approach to digital adoption while maintaining compliance with regulatory
requirements.

* Barrier-repair creams
* Gentle cleansing routines
* Avoiding strong exfoliants

* Injectable treatments
* Facial contouring procedures
* Laser therapies
* Surgical cosmetic procedures
* Microneedling sessions
Swelling is usually most noticeable during the first few days of recovery. Areas around the eyes and
cheeks may appear fuller or tighter than usual. Beauty providers often suggest cold compresses,
hydration, and rest to help reduce puffiness.
Patients are also commonly advised to avoid excessive heat, liquor, or strenuous exercise
immediately after treatment because these activities may increase inflammation. In most cases,
swelling improves gradually as the healing process continues.

Some patients experience temporary breakouts during recovery. This can happen when the skin is

* Chemical exfoliation
* Acne facials
* Retinol treatments
* Deep cleansing procedures
